bug_semantics: joserfc accepted zero-length symmetric key material and passed it to Python's HMAC implementation for HS256, HS384, and HS512 verification. Because an empty HMAC key is public and deterministic, an unauthenticated attacker can compute a matching signature and have jwt.decode accept forged claims whenever application configuration or key lookup supplies an empty secret.
flaw_origin: Commit 29c5a59f4a1bc57b9019e50de56f4b5d5b8280d1 first added HMACAlgorithm.sign and HMACAlgorithm.verify, which passed OctKey.get_op_key output directly to hmac.new without rejecting an empty byte string. OctKey already accepted and returned empty raw material in the immediate parent, but the vulnerable HMAC consumer did not exist there; adding that consumer completed the forgeable verification mechanism.

Official CVE.org record CVE-2026-49852 is PUBLISHED and states that versions before 1.6.8 accept attacker-forged HMAC JWTs when the supplied key is empty; its references name the vendor advisory, fix commit, and 1.6.8 release: https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-49852

The BIC parent tree's src/joserfc/rfc7518/oct_key.py import_key converts strings to bytes and returns OctKey without a length rejection, and get_op_key returns raw_key; thus the BIC's new HMAC consumer receives b'' unchanged.

reasoning: The vulnerability is real and publicly confirmed: an application-provided empty octet key reaches HMAC verification, letting an attacker reproduce the digest and forge JWT claims. The atomic BIC is 29c5a59f4a1bc57b9019e50de56f4b5d5b8280d1 because it first creates the HMAC implementation and writes both unguarded hmac.new calls; although its parent already permits empty OctKey material, that parent lacks the HMAC consumer entirely. git log -L and copy-aware blame follow the same vulnerable lines through later formatting, typing, and path-renaming commits, none of which first created the flaw. The BIC has one parent and no evidence of a squash or finer reconstructable member history, and direct tree comparison proves the vulnerable file absent at the parent. Release topology is coherent: the BIC predates affected tag 1.6.7, fix 86d00910b2b2d2d07503fee9b572906daefab7f1 is absent from 1.6.7 and is the parent of patched tag 1.6.8. The fix directly rejects empty key material at import and at HMAC sign/verify entry. Finally, AI attribution is judged only on the BIC commit object: its human author/committer identity, empty trailer set, and message contain no AI marker. Therefore this is a genuine human-authored vulnerability and the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
